title: disabling alt+tab fails when holding an additional key

judgment.rationale: The disabled-shortcut handler explicitly skips matching when another key is held, even outside the configurable exact-match check; this directly fits the reported Alt+Tab bypass.
evidence: PowerToys 0.102.3101 from the Store; left Alt+Tab mapped to Disabled.
Alt+Tab is blocked alone but executes when a letter or digit is held; a diagnostic ZIP is already supplied.
The author reports Windows 25H2/English US and asks whether this is intended behavior.

Current KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp lines 730–734: !IsKeyboardStateClearExceptShortcut skips both shortcut-to-shortcut and VK_DISABLED mappings; the separate exactMatch condition is earlier in the handler.
No direct #52136 PR was found. The guard makes the bypass source-supported, but policy for intentionally disabled shortcuts still needs maintainer agreement.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify the disabled-shortcut guard and decide whether explicit disable should suppress the target chord independently of unrelated held nonmodifier keys.

proposed_fixes.title: Separate disabled-shortcut matching from remap safety guards
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The unconditional clear-keyboard-state guard includes VK_DISABLED, allowing the original OS chord through whenever another nonmodifier key is held.
plan: Confirm intended Disabled versus exact-match semantics with a focused repro and existing remap tests.
If disable is intended to be inclusive, separate VK_DISABLED handling from shortcut-to-shortcut guard logic while preserving extra keys and modifier release state.
Add tests for held letter/digit, key order, key repeat, left/right Alt and exact-match policy.
verification: Alt+Tab remains blocked for the approved matching policy with unrelated keys held; ordinary shortcut remaps and modifier cleanup remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The exact guard matches the symptom; the unresolved part is the product's desired inclusive-versus-exact disabled-shortcut policy.

actions.label: Approve Separate disabled-shortcut matching from remap safety guards

reproduce.title: Verify reported Keyboard Manager behavior
prerequisites: Use a Windows system supported by the tested PowerToys version.
steps: Map left Alt+Tab to Disabled and verify ordinary Alt+Tab is blocked.
Hold A, then press left Alt+Tab; repeat with a digit.
Repeat with different press/release orders and with exact-match enabled and disabled if exposed.
Confirm unrelated held keys are neither swallowed nor left logically pressed.
reproduce.expected_result: An explicitly disabled chord follows its documented matching policy and cannot unexpectedly activate merely because an unrelated key is held.
